problem: Target-driven visual navigation with deep RL in home scenes suffers from limited camera field of view, concealed target locations and sparse rewards, so navigating to unseen (not currently visible) objects is hard.
motivation: Home environments have complex layouts and objects often hidden inside or on top of other objects. Objects have hierarchical dependency (e.g., a superior object like a table or fridge indicates where an inferior object is likely found), so visible objects can serve as reference cues for reaching unseen targets.
key_idea: Learn a superior-inferior object relationship and encode it in a new reward function so that detecting a superior object of the target yields partial reward and provides spatial guidance.
insight: Shaping the reward with object hierarchy both mitigates reward sparsity and injects spatial priors, giving the RL policy interpretable guidance; the abstract reports larger gains on long episodes (13.5%) than overall (6.5% SR). Details of ablations are not available since only the abstract was provided.
method: Superior-inferior relationship (SIR) model: learns dependency relationships among objects, where superior objects indicate the location of inferior/target objects
New reward function: gives partial reward when the agent detects a superior object of the target, in addition to positive reward on finding the target
Visible-object-as-reference: visible objects serve as cues for navigating toward unseen targets
Deep RL navigation network: policy trained with the shaped reward using the onboard camera only

setting.backbone: deep RL visual navigation network (details not given in abstract)
setting.training_data: trained with RL in AI2-THOR scenes (details not given in abstract)

numbers_note: abstract only; only relative gains reported (6.5% SR gain, 13.5% on long episodes), no absolute numbers
results: In AI2-THOR, SIR achieves a 6.5% gain in success rate over the baseline and a 13.5% improvement on long-episode environments. Baseline is not named in the abstract.
limitations: Evaluated only in AI2-THOR simulation, no real-robot tests stated
Relies on predefined or learned object hierarchy that may not generalize to novel object categories or layouts
